taxonomy:
Here’s a compact taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, organized by the main solving mechanism and puzzle structure.

## 1) Loop-drawing puzzles
Goal: draw one continuous loop under constraints.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop through white circles; straight or turning behavior depends on region.
- **Masyu** — loop through black/white circles with straight/turn rules.
- **Mid-loop** — loop through black circles as midpoints of straight segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop, room-based moon/sun alternation.
- **Nagareru** — directed loop influenced by arrows and wind.
- **Slitherlink** — loop around numbered clues on dot grid.
- **Suraromu** — loop through gates in a prescribed order.
- **Yajilin** — loop plus black-cell placement from directional clues.

## 2) Path / connection puzzles
Goal: connect endpoints, islands, or targets with lines or routes.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges.
- **Numberlink** — connect matching number pairs with non-crossing paths.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles through tracks into countries.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas with sum constraints.
- **Pencils** — draw paths from pencil tips using length clues.

## 3) Shading / coloring puzzles
Goal: color cells black/white or otherwise mark cells to satisfy local/global constraints.

- **Akari** — place bulbs so all white cells are lit.
- **Hitori** — shade duplicates while keeping white cells connected.
- **Heyawake** — shade cells with room and connectivity constraints.
- **Kurodoko** — shade black cells so numbered visibility counts work.
- **Kurotto** — shade cells to match sums around circles.
- **Nurikabe** — form islands and a connected black wall.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint walls to create a maze from S to G.
- **Nurimisaki** — shade to form promontories with line-length clues.
- **Norinori** — place paired black blocks in rooms.
- **Shakashaka** — place triangles so remaining white forms rectangles.
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells so stones “drop” into a valid final state.
- **Usowan** — shade cells with one wrong clue per region.
- **Tilepaint** — color tiles to reveal an outline.
- **Choco Banana** — partition into matching white/gray shapes.
- **Double Choco** — divide into blocks containing matching white/gray areas.
- **Nuritwin** — shade regions into two equal blocks.
- **Chained Block** — fill black-cell blocks into chains with shape uniqueness.

## 4) Number-placement puzzles
Goal: fill cells with numbers under arithmetic, adjacency, or region rules.

- **Sudoku** — classic row/column/block uniqueness.
- **Fillomino** — partition into same-number regions of matching size.
- **Ripple Effect** — room-based consecutive numbers with spacing rules.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with 1..n and arrow max constraints.
- **Juosan** — fill with horizontal/vertical marks under territory counts.
- **Nansuke** — place numbers from a given list into blank cells.
- **Five Cells** — divide into 5-cell blocks with line-count clues.
- **Shikaku** — partition into rectangles matching clue numbers.
- **Evolomino** — build growing blocks along arrow routes.
- **Sashigane** — partition into L-shaped blocks with size clues.
- **Hebi** — place snake numbers 1–5 with directional visibility clues.

## 5) Region partitioning / tiling puzzles
Goal: divide the grid into shapes or regions satisfying size/shape constraints.

- **Shikaku** — rectangles around clues.
- **Sashigane** — L-shaped regions.
- **Five Cells** — 5-cell blocks.
- **Evolomino** — blocks growing by one cell along arrows.
- **Choco Banana** — paired same-shape regions of two colors.
- **Double Choco** — paired same-shape regions of two colors.
- **Nuritwin** — two equal blocks per region.
- **Chained Block** — black-cell polyomino blocks in chains.
- **LITS** — tetromino tiling in rooms.
- **Norinori** — paired black cells in rooms.
- **Tilepaint** — tile regions forming an outline.

## 6) Visibility / line-of-sight puzzles
Goal: use counts based on what can be seen in rows/columns/directions.

- **Akari** — bulbs illuminate until blocked.
- **Kurodoko** — numbers count visible white cells to nearest black/frame.
- **Kurotto** — circles sum continuous black runs in four directions.
- **Hebi** — directional snake visibility clues.
- **Makaro** — arrow points to maximum adjacent number.
- **Ripple Effect** — duplicate spacing in rows/columns.
- **Yajilin** — directional black-cell counts.
- **Nurimisaki** — straight-line white lengths from promontories.
- **Suraromu** — gate-crossing order along loop.
- **Satogaeri** — movement tracks and crossings.

## 7) Connectivity / topology puzzles
Goal: maintain or break connectivity in a controlled way.

- **Akari** — all white cells must be illuminated.
- **Hitori** — white cells must remain connected.
- **Nurikabe** — black wall connected; white islands isolated.
- **Heyawake** — white cells cannot form forbidden separations.
- **LITS** — colored cells connected.
- **Nurimeizu** — white path from S to G with no loops.
- **Yajilin** — loop plus disconnected black cells.
- **Slitherlink** — single loop.
- **Masyu** — single loop with circle constraints.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop through midpoints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop with room alternation.
- **Suraromu** — single loop through gates.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop with region behavior.
- **Nagareru** — directed single loop.

## 8) Hybrid puzzles
These combine multiple mechanisms.

- **Akari** — shading + visibility.
- **Yajilin** — loop + shading.
- **Nurikabe** — shading + connectivity + size.
- **Heyawake** — shading + room counts + connectivity.
- **Kurodoko** — shading + visibility.
- **Masyu** — loop + local turn/straight constraints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop + room alternation.
- **Nurimeizu** — shading + maze/path.
- **Satogaeri** — movement + routing.
- **Makaro** — number placement + directional max.
- **Ripple Effect** — number placement + spacing.
- **Hebi** — number placement + directional visibility.
- **Pencils** — path drawing + length clues.
- **Choco Banana / Double Choco** — partitioning + shape matching.
- **Nuritwin** — partitioning + connectivity.
- **Chained Block** — polyomino shape uniqueness + chain connectivity.

If you want, I can also turn this into:
1. a **table with columns** like “puzzle type / core mechanic / clue style,”  
2. a **hierarchical tree**, or  
3. a **machine-readable JSON taxonomy**.
